key_points: Global leader in loyalty management with 410+ brands including 20 Fortune 500 clients across 47 countries
Strong NRR of 115% with 130% NRR among top 10 customers indicating deep customer relationships
Loyalty+ platform contributes 90% of revenue and enables scalable land-and-expand strategy across adjacent modules
Estimated revenue/EBITDA/PAT CAGR of 25%/53%/132% over FY25-28E
Proven acquisition playbook with 4-year payback period and 20%+ ROIC on acquired assets
AI integration through aiRA (AI-powered Retail Analytics assistant) and AI co-pilots across platform
Transaction-based pricing model reduces exposure to seat-based pricing disruption from AI
Diversified revenue across retail (30%), BFSI, healthcare, CPG and travel verticals reducing concentration risk
Elevated client concentration with top 5 customers contributing 40% of revenue
NRR expected to stabilize in 115-116% range going forward
catalysts: Acquisition integration and synergy realization
Expansion of Loyalty+ into adjacent geographies
AI-driven monetization expansion from existing customer base
Cross-selling of Engage+, Insights+ and Rewards+ modules
Growth in emerging markets particularly Asia-Pacific
Platform migration of acquired customers from on-premises to cloud
reports.summary: Capillary Technologies is positioned as a global leader in loyalty and customer engagement SaaS with a proven acquisition playbook and strong land-and-expand model anchored by its Loyalty+ platform. The company demonstrates resilient growth with 115% NRR, 410+ enterprise clients including Fortune 500 companies, and is actively embedding AI across its platform to drive productivity and monetization. JM Financial initiates coverage with a BUY recommendation and INR 650 target price (20.4% upside), valuing the company at 19x FY28E EBITDA with expected 25%/53%/132% CAGR in revenue/EBITDA/PAT over FY25-28E.

key_points: SOIL metamorphosing from commodity explosives player to India's only large vertically integrated private ammunition and warfare platform
Defence revenues growing at 59% CAGR (FY25-28E) driven by Rs 180 bn order book with 13x book-to-bill ratio
Rs 60.8 bn Pinaka order marks transition to system-level rocket ammunition manufacturing with multi-decade execution opportunity
Three-engine growth model: domestic explosives (43% FY25 revenues), international explosives (38% FY25 revenues), defence (26% FY26E revenues)
Overall revenue CAGR of 25% (FY25-28E) with EPS CAGR of 29% and margin expansion from 26.0% to 27.2%
Export defence order book of Rs 110 bn demonstrates global credibility; presence in 90+ countries with manufacturing in 7+ countries
Strong quality metrics: RoE/RoCE of 28.0%/30.9% projected in FY28E; net debt/equity near zero
Pipeline includes Nagastra loitering munitions, Rudrastra and Vijayastra UAVs, Bhargavastra counter-drone systems, and medium-calibre ammunition
catalysts: Pinaka order execution ramp-up (deliveries commenced in 4QFY26)
Export defence order book execution (Rs 110 bn with 2-6 year timelines)
New product commercialisation: Nagastra-2, Rudrastra, Vijayastra, Bhargavastra
Medium-calibre ammunition production scaling
International customer wins for Pinaka variants (Armenia precedent; Europe and Southeast Asia interest)
Defence export push by Indian government
Global ammunition shortage dynamics
reports.summary: Solar Industries India is undergoing a strategic transformation from a commodity explosives player into India's leading vertically integrated defence and ammunition platform. With a Rs 180 bn defence order book (13x FY25 revenues), landmark Rs 60.8 bn Pinaka contract, and Rs 110 bn export order book, SOIL is positioned for sustained 25% revenue CAGR and 29% EPS CAGR through FY28E. The company's three-engine growth model (domestic explosives, international explosives, defence) combined with strong execution visibility, margin expansion, and a rich product pipeline across loitering munitions, UAVs, and counter-drone systems justifies the 65x valuation multiple and Rs 18,812 target price (21.7% upside).

key_points: Broad-based capex upcycle driven by multiple load vectors: thermal, renewables, transmission, grid storage
Medium-term power demand growth forecast at 5-6% CAGR supported by electrification, data centers, cooling load, policy-backed manufacturing
GENCO capacity additions FY26E-32E will be 2.3-2.5x those of FY19-25, with 97 GW additional coal-based capacity under construction or planning
System focus shifted from capacity deficits to reliability/flexibility; non-solar-hour adequacy now critical challenge
CEA resource adequacy framework flags non-solar-hour power strain risks for next two years
Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 proposes reforms supporting demand growth
Stock preference order: NTPC > Tata Power > PGRD > JSWE; none materially exposed to merchant price volatility
NTPC positioned well with regulated business duration, cost-of-funds advantage, multi-modal generation
Tata Power in multi-year transition with growing lower-volatility T&D and renewables exposure
PGRD direct beneficiary of transmission grid buildout; improved commissioning and capex trajectories
JSWE well-placed for thermal and renewable buildout with contracted core business
catalysts: Stronger power demand pickup
NTPC thermal and nuclear capacity additions
PGCIL transmission project awards and grid expansion
Tata Power discom privatization wins
Tata Power pumped storage plant PPA tie-ups
JSW Energy group captive renewable wins
JSW Energy thermal commissioning timelines by FY30
El Niño-linked demand tailwinds in 2026
National Electricity Policy 2026 implementation
reports.summary: India's power sector is entering a multi-year, multi-vector capex upcycle driven by thermal restart, renewable additions, transmission expansion, and grid storage deployment—addressing shifting challenges from capacity deficits to non-solar-hour flexibility. Medium-term demand growth of 5-6% CAGR is supported by electrification, data centers, cooling loads, and policy-backed manufacturing, with CEA resource adequacy guidelines providing policy anchors. Citi initiates NTPC, PGCIL, Tata Power, and JSW Energy at Buy, with NTPC preferred for its regulated business strength and cost-of-funds advantage.
